label: History
value: Anne Shirley came to Green Gables in Avonlea
unit: Anne Shirley came to Green Gables in Avonlea as an eleven-year-old orphan and was taken in by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert. She made a bosom friend in Diana Barry and threw herself into her studies at Avonlea school, forming a fierce academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe. Under the guidance of Miss Stacy, Anne entered Queen's Academy to earn a teacher's license, sharing top honors with Gilbert. Although she planned to attend college, she chose to stay in Avonlea to care for Marilla and teach locally, during which time she helped found the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Later, she attended Redmond College in Kingsport alongside friends like Priscilla Grant and Philippa Gordon, living at Patty's Place and continuing her education while also teaching during breaks.

value: Anthony was taken in as an orphan.

From his first day, he looked upon his new teacher with hostility and contempt, believing female teachers were useless. He engaged in mischievous acts, such as pouring slate-bottle water down Aurelia Clay's neck and ignoring gentle lectures about acting like a gentleman. Eventually, after a stunt involving a mouse in Anne's desk drawer, Anne lost her temper and whipped him with a pointer, causing his bravado to fail and bringing him to tears.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina was born.
unit: Aunt Jamesina was born a month after her father James drowned at sea. She grew up longing for a yellow silk dress, but neither her mother nor her husband permitted her to buy one. She eventually raised a daughter, Elizabeth, who previously wrote stories before marrying and leaving for the foreign mission field in India. Left alone in a large house, Aunt Jamesina moved to Patty's Place in Kingsport to keep house for Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Phil Gordon, and Stella Maynard. She cared for the household and three cats—Rusty, Joseph, and the Sarah-cat—while remaining worried about her daughter facing snakes in India.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews lived in Avonlea.
unit: Billy Andrews lived in Avonlea and drove a double-seated buggy, taking Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and his sister Jane to a concert at White Sands. During the trip, he insisted that Anne ride on the front seat with him because he admired her immensely and felt proud to drive with her. After his father gave him the upper farm in his own name, Billy sought to get married. Too shy to propose to Anne himself, he badgered his sister Jane until she agreed to ask Anne on his behalf. Upon being rejected, Billy did not break his heart and instead married Nettie Blewett, whom his mother favored and whom he liked as well. He later proudly brought his new bride to church to sit in the Harmon Andrews pew.

label: History
value: Charlotta came to live at Echo Lodge
unit: Charlotta came to live at Echo Lodge to serve Miss Lavendar Lewis for board and clothes. She proved to be the best and most tolerant of the Bowman sisters regarding Miss Lavendar's imaginative pretenses. While working at Echo Lodge, she became fond of regular guests Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, warmly welcoming them whenever they visited. When Miss Lavendar fell into low spirits, Charlotta voiced her deep worries to Anne after accidentally breaking an heirloom bowl without receiving a scolding. Following Miss Lavendar's wedding, Charlotta moved with her and her new husband to Boston, where she felt terribly homesick. She later returned to Echo Lodge during summer vacations as a fully grown-up young lady.

value: Diana Barry lived with her parents
unit: Diana Barry lived with her parents at Orchard Slope in Avonlea. As a child, she met Anne Shirley and swore an oath of lifelong friendship with her, becoming her intimate chum. Later, she became the treasurer of the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. After a courtship with Fred Wright, Diana married him in a ceremony where her father walked her down the aisle, after which the couple drove away to their new home.

label: History
value: Dora's father died when Dora was an infant.
unit: Dora and her twin brother Davy were orphaned at a young age after their father died in their infancy and their sick mother, Mary, passed away. Marilla Cuthbert brought the twins to Green Gables to adopt them. Dora quickly distinguished herself as a neat, well-behaved model child who assisted dutifully with household chores like wiping dishes, feeding chickens, and picking up chips. Unlike her mischievous brother, she excelled in discipline and recited her Sunday lessons like a machine. When given a plot of ground for a garden, she planted and tended orderly rows of vegetables and flowers. During a frightening hail storm, Dora remained calm and composed beside Anne. She later started attending school, where a classmate's ghost stories briefly frightened her from going to bed alone in the dark.

Dora quickly distinguished herself as a neat, well-behaved model child who assisted dutifully with household chores like wiping dishes, feeding chickens, and picking up chips. Unlike her mischievous brother, she excelled in discipline and recited her Sunday lessons like a machine. When given a plot of ground for a garden, she planted and tended orderly rows of vegetables and flowers. During a frightening hail storm, Dora remained calm and composed beside Anne. She later started attending school, where a classmate's ghost stories briefly frightened her from going to bed alone in the dark.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea
unit: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea after spending three years in Alberta with his father. Upon re-entering school, he entered a intense, friendly academic rivalry with Anne Shirley. After attending Queen's Academy together and taking the Second Year work in one year, Gilbert took a job teaching at White Sands to earn money for college, graciously giving up the Avonlea school post to Anne. In Avonlea, he co-founded and served as president of the Avonlea Village Improvement Society.

label: History
value: Gilbert attended Redmond College
unit: Gilbert later attended Redmond College alongside Anne. There, he led the Freshmen to victory in the Arts Rush, was elected Freshman Class President, and became Captain of the Freshman football team. During his sophomore year, he confessed his love to Anne, but she rejected his marriage proposal. Afterwards, he maintained a courteous distance while working during summers at the Daily News office. He later escorted Christine Stuart at the request of her brother, sparking college rumors of an engagement. After graduating with High Honors in Classics and winning the Cooper Prize, Gilbert suffered a severe case of typhoid fever from overwork, but safely recovered, ultimately reconciling with Anne.

After a severe dispute, Emily left him, and Mr. Harrison moved to Prince Edward Island to live as an old bachelor next to the Cuthbert farm. Months after his arrival, his wife Emily rejoined him in Avonlea, and they reconciled. After a severe dispute, Emily left him, and Mr. Harrison moved to Prince Edward Island to live as an old bachelor next to the Cuthbert farm. Initially labeled a crank by the locals for his eccentricities and erratic housekeeping, he gradually struck up a warm friendship with Anne Shirley. Months after his arrival, his wife Emily rejoined him in Avonlea, and they reconciled. Following their reunion, Mr. Harrison became a regular churchgoer, dressed neatly, and maintained warm ties with his neighbors, while continuing to give straightforward advice to Anne on her writing.

Upon completing her studies, she became a schoolteacher at Newbridge, while also serving as a founding member and active committee chairman in the Avonlea Voluntary Improvement Society. She later went west to teach on the western prairies. Upon returning home, she became engaged to Mr. Inglis, a Winnipeg millionaire, planning a wedding tour to Europe and a life in a mansion.

value: Josie attended Avonlea school
unit: Josie attended Avonlea school alongside Anne Shirley and her classmates. She frequently traded dares with other students, successfully walking a board fence after daring Jane Andrews to hop on one leg, and later daring Anne Shirley to walk a ridgepole. When Miss Stacy organized recitations and dialogues, Josie was sulky because she was denied the role of fairy queen due to her stout figure. She later caused a three-month feud with Julia Bell after repeating a mean comment about Julia's reciting bow. At the exhibition, she won first prize for her knitted lace. She joined the Queen's class to prepare for entrance exams, stating she intended to go to college for education's sake since she would not need to earn a living. She attended Queen's Academy in the Second Class work, earning a reputation as the sharpest-tongued student there. Following her studies, she continued her education alongside her Avonlea peers, maintaining her taunting attitude toward Anne Shirley and accusing Anne of copying her prize-winning story.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis lived a quiet life at Echo Lodge.
unit: Lavendar Lewis lived a quiet life at Echo Lodge, cared for by a series of young Bowman handmaidens, whom she collectively addressed as Charlotta. She struck up a close friendship with Anne Shirley and Diana Barry when they stumbled upon her home, finding a kindred spirit in Anne. Later, after meeting Stephen Irving's young son Paul, Stephen returned to her life after twenty-five years apart. The two reconciled their old romance and were married in an informal outdoor ceremony in her garden at Echo Lodge, afterwards moving together to Boston.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet life.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet, cramped life at Green Gables in Avonlea with her brother Matthew. In middle age, they decided to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, but due to a mistake, Anne Shirley was brought to them instead; despite initial hesitation, Marilla chose to keep and raise Anne. Over the years, Marilla strictly supervised Anne's upbringing and domestic training while growing deeply attached to her in secret. Following Matthew's death and her own failing eyesight, Marilla took in her orphaned distant relatives, the twins Davy and Dora Keith, taking charge of their discipline and welfare. As Anne grew into womanhood and went off to college, Marilla continued to manage Green Gables with the assistance of Mrs. Rachel Lynde, remaining devotedly attached to Anne.

label: History
value: Paul Irving came from Boston.
unit: Paul Irving came from Boston to live with his grandmother in Avonlea. Upon starting at the Avonlea school, he quickly formed an intense bond with his teacher, Anne Shirley, who recognized him as a kindred spirit and a child of genius. He entertained himself by creating rich imaginary companions known as his rock people, including Nora and the Twin Sailors. Paul defended his American heritage in a drawn fight against St. Clair Donnell and protected the younger boys at school. He later formed a friendship with Miss Lavendar Lewis, bonding over their shared imaginative minds. When his father, Stephen Irving, unexpectedly arrived in Avonlea, Paul was overjoyed and supported his father's reunion and eventual marriage to Miss Lavendar. Even as he grew older and reached sixteen, his close connection and kindred spirit with Anne remained unchanged.

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon enrolled at Redmond College.
unit: Philippa Gordon enrolled at Redmond College, where she immediately established herself as the class beauty and social belle. She quickly befriended Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant, introducing them to her extensive social circle. During her early college years, she struggled to choose between two home-town suitors, Alec and Alonzo. Later, she moved into Patty's Place with Anne, Priscilla, and Stella Maynard, where she learned basic household duties. While spending a summer month at Prospect Point, she met Jonas Blake, a minister and Redmond graduate, with whom she fell in love. Despite her mother's initial resistance, Philippa remained firm in her choice, took the Johnson Scholarship in Mathematics to impress him, and earned his love. She was married to Jonas in June, with Anne serving as her bridesmaid, and subsequently wrote a letter to Gilbert Blythe that encouraged him to pursue Anne again.

She quickly befriended Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant, introducing them to her extensive social circle. During her early college years, she struggled to choose between two home-town suitors, Alec and Alonzo. Later, she moved into Patty's Place with Anne, Priscilla, and Stella Maynard, where she learned basic household duties. While spending a summer month at Prospect Point, she met Jonas Blake, a minister and Redmond graduate, with whom she fell in love. Despite her mother's initial resistance, Philippa remained firm in her choice, took the Johnson Scholarship in Mathematics to impress him, and earned his love. She was married to Jonas in June, with Anne serving as her bridesmaid, and subsequently wrote a letter to Gilbert Blythe that encouraged him to pursue Anne again.

value: Mr. Phillips served as the school teacher in Avonlea.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the school teacher in Avonlea. During his tenure, he regularly instructed pupils such as Anne Shirley, Gilbert Blythe, and Prissy Andrews, though he often mortified and disciplined students harshly. He routinely spent time helping Prissy Andrews with her studies in the evenings and publicly favored her, giving her Mayflowers and sending away to town for carnations for her performance. label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Stella Maynard, becoming close friends with them. While a student, Mr. Phillips wrote verses dedicated to her. After graduating, she taught school at Carmody before taking her own home school. During this period, she wrote a paper on cemeteries for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and arranged a visit to Green Gables with her famous aunt, Mrs. Charlotte E. Morgan. After obtaining her father's consent, she entered Redmond College with Anne Shirley, and the two boarded together during their freshman year. In her sophomore year, Priscilla moved into Patty's Place along with Anne, Philippa Gordon, Stella Maynard, and Aunt Jamesina. During her summer break, she went to Avonlea to visit Anne at Green Gables. In her final year at Redmond, she focused her studies heavily on classics, preparing alongside her housemates for graduation.

value: Rachel Lynde is a capable woman.
unit: Rachel Lynde is a capable, hardworking, and outspoken woman who prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor. label: History
value: Jonas Blake graduated from Redmond College
unit: Jonas Blake graduated from Redmond College and later studied theology at St. Columbia. For a summer, he took charge of the Point Prospect Mission Church, where he met Philippa Gordon and quickly became close companions with her while fishing, boating, and walking together. Although he resisted entering the ministry for a long time, he eventually recognized it as his duty. He visited Patty's Place frequently while studying, becoming a general favorite. After graduating from St. Columbia, he visited Philippa's parents at Mount Holly and won their approval despite initial reluctance from her mother. They were married in June, after which he planned to pastor a small mission church on Patterson Street in the slums.

label: History
value: Roy Gardner attended Redmond College
unit: Roy Gardner attended Redmond College before being forced to give up his class two years prior to travel abroad with his sick mother. Upon his return, he resumed his studies at Redmond and actively courted Anne Shirley. He won over most residents at Patty's Place with his charm and courtesy, though he teased the Sarah-cat, who disliked him. During his courtship, he sent Anne orchids, violets, poetry, and regular letters, becoming widely expected by college social circles to propose to her. However, when he proposed, Anne rejected him, leaving him pale and looking foolish as he had felt very confident of her acceptance.

value: > It—it won’t be very long now, Anne. I feel sure of that. And I’d rather have you than any one else. I always liked you best of all the girls I went to school with. value: Ruby grew up in Avonlea.

She spent her final summer at home, coming to terms with her terminal illness, before dying peacefully in her sleep.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired as the new teacher for Avonlea school.
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired as the new teacher for Avonlea school, becoming the town's first female teacher. Upon taking charge, she introduced physical culture exercises every morning and evening, bi-weekly Friday afternoon recitations, and field days in the woods to study nature. She also taught her pupils proper speech and corrected common grammatical errors. During her tenure, she prepared a group of pupils known as the Queen's class for their Entrance examinations, encouraging them to pursue higher studies. Although offered a position in her home district's grade school after her first year, she returned to Avonlea to complete her term before her rule at the school came to an end at the close of June.

unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired as the new teacher for Avonlea school, becoming the town's first female teacher. Upon taking charge, she introduced physical culture exercises every morning and evening, bi-weekly Friday afternoon recitations, and field days in the woods to study nature. She also taught her pupils proper speech and corrected common grammatical errors. During her tenure, she prepared a group of pupils known as the Queen's class for their Entrance examinations, encouraging them to pursue higher studies. Although offered a position in her home district's grade school after her first year, she returned to Avonlea to complete her term before her rule at the school came to an end at the close of June.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard became intimate friends with Anne Shirley while studying at Queen's Academy.
unit: While studying at Queen's Academy, Stella Maynard became intimate friends with Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant, forming a close circle of ambitious students. After completing her studies at Queen's, where she was considered the most beautiful student in the Second Year classes, she taught school. Later, she conceived the idea of attending Redmond College and renting Patty's Place to live with Anne, Priscilla, and her aunt, who served as housekeeper. At Redmond, she joined her housemates—along with Philippa Gordon—at Patty's Place as a student, eventually earning a good all-round showing in her examinations.
